sources.entry: Archivator - Menu bar archive tool that compresses and extracts files by dragging them onto a radial wheel. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/davidpraznik/Archivator) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: A macOS menu bar app that compresses or extracts files by dragging them onto a radial wheel while holding the Option key.
summary.what_it_does: Archivator runs in the macOS menu bar. While dragging files or folders from Finder, holding Option opens a radial wheel at the cursor; dropping onto a segment compresses the items to ZIP, 7Z, or TAR.GZ. If everything dragged is an archive, the wheel instead offers "Extract here" (into a new folder beside the archive) or "Extract to…" to pick a folder. Supported extraction formats are ZIP, 7Z, TAR, TGZ, GZ, BZ2, XZ, and RAR. Results are saved next to the originals, and name collisions get a number appended so existing files are never overwritten. Esc cancels a running job, and the trigger key can be switched to Control or Control+Option in Settings. Extraction uses the system tar (libarchive) with path-safety checks that refuse ".." entries and links pointing outside the target folder.
use_cases: compress files from Finder via drag and drop
extract archives without opening a separate app
create ZIP or 7Z archives from the menu bar
unpack RAR, BZ2, or XZ files on a Mac
extract an archive into a new folder next to it
how_to_run: Clone the repository and open Archivator.xcodeproj in Xcode.
Build and run the project from Xcode.
Start Archivator; it appears in the menu bar.
Drag files from Finder while holding Option, then drop on a wheel segment.
notable: Radial wheel UI opened by holding Option during a drag
Extracts many formats including RAR, 7Z, XZ, and BZ2
Never overwrites; appends numbers to duplicate names
Path traversal and symlink escape protection during extraction
Configurable trigger key that coexists with the Konverter app
caveats: Builds from GitHub are not notarized, so macOS blocks first launch and requires a manual Open Anyway step
Requires macOS 14.6 or later; tested only on macOS 27
